literal: 'Alas!' saying, things that cause regret, do not do; if one does, then, such things not doing again is good.
translation: Do not perform deeds that will make you cry out in regret, 'Alas, what have I done!' If you happen to commit such a mistake, it is best never to repeat it again.
modern: 'ஐயோ! என்ன காரியம் செய்தேன்!' என்று வருந்தக்கூடிய செயல்களைச் செய்யக்கூடாது. ஒருவேளை அப்படிச் செய்துவிட்டால், மீண்டும் அத்தகைய செயல்களைச் செய்யாமல் இருப்பது நல்லது.
explanation: This couplet from the chapter on Purity of Action advises against performing deeds that lead to remorse. The word 'eṟṟu' is an exclamation of grief or regret, used when one realizes a mistake. The poet warns that one should not do things that cause such regret ('iraṅkuva'). However, if a person does commit such an act ('ceyvāṉēl'), the best course of action is to ensure they never repeat ('ceyyāmai') such deeds ('aṉṉa') again ('maṟṟu').
